_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 30 (the rest of Jacob's sons; striped/spotted flocks). Saadia-specific: v.2 'אמן דון אללה' = 'am I in place of God' (preserves the rhetorical force); v.14 'לפאח' = 'mandrakes' (Saadia uses lufāḥ — the standard medieval Arabic name for mandrake); v.32-43 the striped/spotted/dappled terminology rendered carefully: 'מנקטה' = spotted/dotted, 'מחגלה' = striped/banded (lit. 'with anklets'), 'בלקא' = piebald, 'חמא' = brown/dark; v.41 'אלרביעייה' / 'אלכ'ריפייה' = 'spring' / 'autumn' (Saadia interprets המקושרות/העטופים — strong/feeble — as seasonally categorized).

translations.1: And when Rachel saw that she had not borne to Jacob, she envied her sister, and said to him: 'Grant me a child, or else I am dead.'
translations.2: And his anger flared against her; and he said: 'Am I in place of God, who has held back the fruit of the womb from you?'
translations.3: She said: 'Behold my maidservant Bilhah; come to her — let her bear upon my knees, and let my house also be built up from her.'
translations.4: And she gave him Bilhah her maidservant for a wife; and Jacob came in to her.
translations.5: And Bilhah conceived, and bore him a son.
translations.6: And Rachel said: 'God has judged in my favor; and He has also heard my voice, and granted me a son.' Therefore she named him Dan.
translations.7: And Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, conceived again, and bore a second son to Jacob.
translations.8: And Rachel said: 'A turning from God — I have turned with my sister, and I have prevailed.' And she named him Naphtali.
translations.9: And when Leah saw that she had ceased from bearing, she took Zilpah her maidservant, and gave her to Jacob for a wife.
translations.10: And Zilpah bore him a son.
translations.11: And she said: 'The news has come true!' And she named him Gad.
translations.12: And Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore Jacob a second son.
translations.13: And Leah said: 'From my description — that the women shall describe me.' And she named him Asher.
translations.14: Then Reuben went out, in the days of the wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the wilderness; and he brought them to Leah his mother. And Rachel said to her: 'Give me some of them.'
translations.15: She said to her: 'Was it not enough that you took my husband, that you would also take my son's mandrakes?' Rachel said: 'Then he shall lie with you tonight, in exchange for that.'
translations.16: And when Jacob came from the wilderness in the evening, Leah went out to meet him, and said: 'Come in to me — for I have rightfully purchased you with my son's mandrakes.' And he lay with her that night.
translations.17: And God heard her; and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son.
translations.18: And she said: 'God has given me my wage — because I gave my maidservant to my husband.' And she named him Issachar.
translations.19: And Leah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
translations.20: She said: 'God has endowed me with a goodly endowment; this time my husband shall dwell with me, for I have borne him six sons.' And she named him Zebulun.
translations.21: And after that she bore a daughter, and named her Dinah.
translations.22: Then God remembered Rachel; and He heard her, and granted her a child.
translations.23: And she conceived, and bore a son; and she said: 'God has taken away my reproach.'
translations.24: And she named him Joseph, saying: 'God shall add to me another son.'
translations.25: And when Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban: 'Send me away, that I may go to my place and to my land.
translations.26: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, that I may go; for you know my service which I have served you.'
translations.27: And Laban said to him: 'If I have found favor with you — for I have tested, and God has blessed me on your account.'
translations.28: And he said: 'Specify to me your wage, that I may give it.'
translations.29: And he said to him: 'You know how I have served you, and how your cattle have fared with me.
translations.30: For it was little that you had before me, and it has spread out into much; and God has blessed you on my account. And now — when shall I, too, do for my own house?'
translations.31: He said: 'What shall I give you?' Jacob said: 'You shall give me nothing — but if you do for me this thing, I shall return to pasture your flock, and to keep it:
translations.32: I shall pass through all your flock today, and remove from it every speckled and piebald lamb, and every brown head among the sheep, and every piebald and speckled one among the goats. And that shall be my wage.
translations.33: And my honesty shall witness for me tomorrow, when I come to claim my wage before you: every one which is not speckled or piebald among the goats, or brown among the sheep — it shall be reckoned stolen by me.'
translations.34: Laban said: 'Yes — would that it be as you have said.'
translations.35: But on that day he removed the striped and speckled male goats, and all the speckled and piebald she-goats — every one that had any white in it — and every brown one among the sheep; and he gave them into the hand of his sons.
translations.36: And he set a distance of three days' journey between himself and Jacob; and Jacob pastured the rest of Laban's flock.
translations.37: Then Jacob took fresh poplar rods, and almond, and plane-tree; and he peeled white peelings on them — until he exposed the white that was on them.
translations.38: And he set the rods which he had peeled in the troughs, in the watering channels — so that the sheep, when they came to drink, would be facing them, and would conceive at that time.
translations.39: And the flocks conceived by the rods; and they bore striped and speckled and piebald.
translations.40: And Jacob set the sheep apart; and he set at the head of the flock every striped one, and every brown one in Laban's flock; and he set for himself flocks alone, and did not put them together with Laban's flock.
translations.41: And in every time when the early-spring flocks were in heat, Jacob would set the rods opposite them in the troughs, that they should conceive by them.
translations.42: And when the autumn ones came — he would not set them; and the autumn-born became Laban's, and the spring-born Jacob's.
translations.43: And the man grew exceedingly rich; and he had many sheep, and maidservants and slaves, and camels and donkeys.
